title: U.S. House · Florida's 7th District
area: East-central Florida, including parts of Volusia, Seminole and Orange counties.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Cory Mills did not win the August 18, 2026 Republican primary, which Ryan Elijah won over Michael Johnson and Sarah Ulrich. Bale Dalton won the Democratic primary over Alan Grayson and Marialana Kinter. Christopher Dennison (Libertarian) also qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Ryan Elijah
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary over incumbent Cory Mills, Michael Johnson and Sarah Ulrich.

summary.text: Ryan Elijah is the Republican nominee for the open Florida 7th Congressional District seat. A longtime television news anchor, most recently at FOX 35 Orlando, he left that job in 2026 to run and won the August 18 Republican primary over incumbent Rep. Cory Mills. According to his campaign website, he is running on lower taxes, reduced federal spending, support for law enforcement and school choice.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Anderson University in 1994.
Worked as a television news anchor; his most recent position was at FOX 35 Orlando, which he left in April 2026 to run for Congress.
According to his candidate survey, he served as a public figure in the community for 14 years, and he and his wife raised their sons in the district.
Says he comes from a military family; his campaign website says his father and grandfather both served.
Announced his candidacy on April 28, 2026 and won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary, defeating incumbent Rep. Cory Mills.
Describes himself as active in his church; his campaign website lists him as pro-life and a supporter of the Second Amendment.

priorities.text: Lowering taxes and cutting wasteful government spending and fraud.
Reducing healthcare regulation to lower costs and premiums.
Supporting law enforcement, including federal funding for training and technology and tougher penalties for assaulting officers.

positions.summary: Says he is a fiscal conservative who will fight to keep taxes low and reduce federal spending and debt.
Says he will push for federal funding for law-enforcement training, technology and personnel, and support tougher penalties for assaulting or shooting officers.

candidates.name: Bale Dalton
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Alan Grayson and Marialana Kinter.

summary.text: Bale Dalton is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 7th Congressional District seat. A U.S. Naval Academy graduate and Navy helicopter pilot with over 24 years in the Navy and Navy Reserve, he later worked for Sen. Bill Nelson and served as NASA Chief of Staff. He won the August 18 Democratic primary with 45.6% of the vote and, per his candidate survey, is campaigning on costs such as gas, health care premiums, housing and property insurance.

background.text: Says he was born and raised in Central Florida and has spent his career in public service.

Graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy and served over 24 years in the Navy and Navy Reserve, including 13 years active duty as a helicopter pilot, deploying to Iraq, Afghanistan, the Horn of Africa and the Pacific.

As a Navy helicopter pilot, he says he flew search and rescue flights after Hurricane Katrina, medical evacuation missions in Kuwait, and special operations missions in Iraq and Africa, and directed combat air support with Navy SEALs in Afghanistan.
Worked for Sen. Bill Nelson helping Florida veterans access care and benefits, then returned to active duty as commanding officer of a Navy special-operations support helicopter squadron.
Worked at an aerospace company in the private sector, where he says he used his military background to improve efficiency and operations.
Served as NASA Chief of Staff, managing 16,500 employees.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.6% of the vote, ahead of Marialana Kinter and Alan Grayson.

priorities.text: Says his top priority is making Florida affordable again, addressing gas, health care, housing and insurance costs.
Wants to make it illegal for members of Congress to trade stocks in companies they regulate.
Wants to restore Medicaid and Medicare funding and reverse premium increases, and supports negotiating prescription drug prices.

positions.summary: Says Congress made health care worse by cutting Medicaid and Medicare and raising premiums, and calls for restoring that funding, negotiating drug prices, and building on the Affordable Care Act.
Calls for reversing what he describes as the tariffs predecessor Cory Mills voted for, saying they squeeze small businesses and raise supply-chain costs.

candidates.name: Christopher Dennison
candidates.ballotNote: Libertarian primary was canceled; advanced unopposed.

summary.text: Christopher Dennison is the Libertarian Party nominee for the open Florida 7th Congressional District seat. Little biographical information about him is publicly documented.

background.text: Was unopposed for the Libertarian nomination; the August 18, 2026 Libertarian primary was canceled.

candidates.researchNotes: Checked Christopher Dennison's own Ballotpedia page (https://ballotpedia.org/Christopher_Dennison, no completed 2026 Candidate Connection survey, no campaign website listed) and a web search; a Seminole County Chamber candidate forum report (mynews13.com, August 2026) notes only that Dennison did not attend. No campaign website, biography, or policy statements were found.
